current_quest.name: The List
current_quest.on_the_page: The Confessors' list of the Faithless at Saint Ysolde's was read aloud at the inn in Coldmere; Hollis's name is second on it, and asked who was first, Wren only looked at Darrow. Rae Thorne, who drives the House's last cart, heard it read and climbed through the night to bring it up. While Old Mercy, the sanctuary bell, rings at dawn and dusk, no blade may climb the Steps or pass the gate; miss one ringing and the law lapses till the next. At Darrow's word the winch-brothers have carried a story down to the valley, that the Faithless went down the far side a week ago, and Mother Ione has held Old Mercy since the council, because a bell rung for nobody tells the valley there's somebody. When the grey cloaks are at the bars, Darrow is to tell Wren when. They came in three bells early: six grey cloaks, their cart and a censer are at the winch-house at the foot of the Steps, and one of them sits on Rae's cart with his boots on the board. Rae could have gone down past them while the road was open, and did not. In the hour before dusk four of them climbed to the gate. Confessor Ivo Marrant read the writ at the bars to the House standing in the court, Darrow first, Hollis second, the far cots not read, and asked for the wicket under the law of guests; two grey cloaks came through it before Old Mercy rang, late, and were put back out. Mother Ione spoke the law of names: while the bell rings, no name under it is taken down against its will. Marrant has camped on the lower terrace below the gate, where the springs steam, and called up for the Captain of the Ninth to come down and kneel. He says he will wait.
current_quest._about: on_the_page is what the site shows and must be supported by the chronicle; the GM's own summary lives in saga/state/_gm/plan.json (quest_summary)

current_struggle: The soft season. The knee feels well, and Maelis says that is exactly the danger: the thread is softest now, and the quiet is a liar. He can walk to the chapel and back without the stick; he cannot kneel, and he has asked fifteen times to go down the Steps and been told no fifteen times, the last at the Prior's council. At the wicket his shoulder gave and the knee said one thing, quite clearly; Maelis looked at it afterwards and said nothing, which was worse.
last_beat: Confessor Ivo Marrant read the list at the bars, Darrow first and Hollis second, and asked for the wicket under the law of guests. Darrow read him and said "Wren. Now."; two grey cloaks came through before Old Mercy rang, late, and the House's shoulders put them back out, his own giving. The Prior spoke the law of names. Marrant thanked her for her candour, made his camp on the lower terrace, and called up for the Captain of the Ninth to come down and kneel: he would wait.

maelis.note: has told him what she dared, and not where she learned it; the Confessor's eyes found her at the gate

hollis.note: second on the list, read at the bars; dry, and has told Darrow so; saw him move at his name

wren.note: afraid; hides it with numbers; ran for the bell on his word

choices.text: Tell the lay brothers the Faithless went down the far side a week ago. Let the valley carry it.

inventory: a borrowed stick he refuses to use

recaps._about: One-line 'previously' per chapter file slug, shown at the top of that chapter in the reader. Spoiler-free; only what earlier chapters showed.
recaps.01-the-confessor-at-the-steps: At Harrow Ford the Grace went out of the Ninth Lance in mid-river and did not come back, and Darrow's knee gave way with no blade near it. Carried up the Thousand Steps to Saint Ysolde's, he chose Maelis Vorne's Binding over kneeling again at the Oathspire.
recaps.02-the-grey-cot: In the hour before dusk the grey cloaks climbed to the gate and Confessor Ivo Marrant read his list to the House, Darrow's name first. Two of his men came through the wicket before Old Mercy rang, late, and were put back out; the Prior spoke the law of names, and Marrant made his camp on the lower terrace below the gate, saying he would wait for the Captain of the Ninth to come down and kneel.
